exposure: postpartum temperature exposure (mean temperature, diurnal temperature range, maximum temperature, minimum temperature)
cohort: The study included 429,839 pregnancies from Kaiser Permanente Southern California electronic health records, with mothers having a mean age of 30.22 years.
finding: Maternal exposure to higher temperature and diurnal temperature variability during the postpartum period was associated with an increased risk of postpartum depression, with effect modification by maternal age, race/ethnicity, air pollution, green space, and air conditioning penetration.
